teaser.en: Flip a leaf of this bush tree and it flashes silver, lined with fine veins as neat as ruled paper.

summary.en: *Msalasanga* is the broad-leaved resin tree, a bush shrub with silvery-backed leaves and a creamy resin. Its dark red wood is durable, and its bark, roots and twigs are used as medicine.

about.en: *Msalasanga* is a shrub or small tree with leathery leaves in groups of three. The undersides are silvery, crossed by fine, closely spaced parallel veins, so a breeze turning the leaves makes the crown shimmer. Cut the bark and a creamy resin oozes out. The small fruits are black and kidney-shaped.

where.en: It grows in coastal bushland and wooded grassland.

uses.en: The wood is dark red and durable. Bark, roots and twigs are used in traditional medicine, much as for its relative *Ozoroa insignis*.

names.en: Pakia records two Digo names, *msalasanga* and *msangasanga*; the second is shared with Duruma, and ICRAF gives *msalasanga*. In Swahili it is *mwaalika*, and in Giriama *mukuikwaiyu*. In English it is the broad-leaved resin tree.

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
